cards.title: Debugger step 2: native DAP/lldb backend (full-feature stepping + editor wiring)
cards.body: D-DBG3 step 2 (the in-session command surface shipped in c52 over the interpreter). Remaining: a native backend that steps the FULL feature set the interpreter declines (E2203: FFI, tasks, #Unsafe, native std), the D-DBG2 --raw-frames expert view, and editor DAP wiring (VS Code/Zed). The ratified command vocabulary (step/next/continue/finish/break/print/locals/backtrace) is fixed and reused; only the native backend + protocol transport remain.
cards.plan: Implement the complete ratified D-DBG-DAP1=A profile as one projection of the existing debugger model. Preserve the shipped std-only lldb backend, Inferior transport, line map, terminal commands, and DAP stdio skeleton, then close every missing protocol capability in crates/jet-debug. Enforce strict byte-counted Content-Length framing, positive correlated sequence IDs, bounded JSON, one response per accepted request, Jet-owned structured errors, and the Start to Initialized to Configuring to Stopped or Running to Terminated state machine; no user code runs before configurationDone and advertised capabilities equal behavior. Support launch args, cwd, env; verified same-user local attach; replacement source breakpoints with conditions, hit counts, and logpoints; all-stop Jet-task threads; Jet-only stacks, scopes, nested variables; bounded read-only Jet evaluation; panic, error, and signal filters; pause; restart; cancellation; progress; timeouts; ordered output; and exact exit or signal status. Attach verifies process identity, executable build ID, source hashes, architecture, image, and matching jetmap before target mutation. Disconnect terminates launched targets and continues attached targets. Restart rebuilds through the same pipeline, preserves source breakpoints, and invalidates every object reference. Default output hides generated Rust, helpers, backend values, addresses, secrets, and raw text; explicit showRawFrames appends marked raw frames and scopes without changing semantics. Truthfully reject mutation, memory access, reverse execution, disassembly, remote transport, reverse requests, telemetry, and every unsupported request. Vendor a pinned Microsoft DAP schema; model-test every legal and illegal state transition and reference lifetime; drive current VS Code and Zed clients plus live native lldb without skip on supported Linux/macOS hosts using production FFI/task programs. Bound and reap adapter, debugger, launched, and attached processes on every failure. No new syntax or dependency gate.

log.text: Heads-up for planning: after D-ONECORE1=A (#778), jet run stacks can mix native Cranelift frames and interpreter (tier-0) frames. The native DAP backend must present mixed-tier stacks coherently — plan a frame-provenance seam, not lldb-only assumptions.

The Open Owner-Q ask below is now resolved — owner said add it.

[done] Native lldb backend shipped end-to-end and verified against a REAL live lldb (fetched via nixpkgs for this session; not yet in flake.nix devShell — see Open Owner-Q). Codegen: TStmt::LineMarker + emit_bundle_dbg/compile_for_debug emit `// jet:line N` markers gated by cx.debug_linemap (off by default — zero effect on normal builds, golden tests, or the JIT tier; confirmed via full test suite + `cargo test --workspace` diffing). New Source/Debug/{LineMap,Inferior,Native,Dap}.rs. `jet debug` auto-dispatches interpreter vs native via the SAME E2203 boundary scan (needs_native) — one command, one meaning (I8); `--dap` forces native for editor launch; `--raw-frames` (D-DBG2) shows raw Rust file:line. Reuses the exact ratified (jet) vocabulary (D-DBG3) over both backends. Live-lldb verification surfaced and fixed THREE real bugs a docs-only implementation would have shipped broken: (1) lldb never re-prints a bare prompt over a pipe (echoes command instead) — naive prompt-wait hangs forever, fixed with a sentinel-command read loop; (2) a resume command's own stop banner is asynchronous and can lose a race to the NEXT command's reply — fixed by always deriving position from a synchronous follow-up `bt`, never the resume's own text; (3) the debuggee inherits lldb's stdout by default, so a Jet `print()` can tear a control-channel sentinel in half — fixed by redirecting debuggee stdout/stderr to temp files via `settings set target.output/error-path` and draining them into the transcript. Also loads rustc's own Rust pretty-printer (lldb_lookup.py + lldb_commands, same two files rust-lldb loads) so String/&str locals render as `"text"` instead of raw allocator internals. Tests: 12 new unit tests (LineMap/Inferior, no lldb needed) + tests/debug_native.rs (5 tests, gated on lldb presence like tests/observe.rs gates on rustc — skips clean without it). New example examples/features/189_debug_native.jet (native-only via `use core.fs`) + golden .out. Full regression pass: cargo build/test workspace-relevant targets (debug, debug_native, golden, observe, cli, tir, decisions, dev/JIT) all green. NOT done: DAP JSON-over-stdio server (Dap.rs) is implemented to the documented wire spec but UNTESTED against a real editor (no VS Code/Zed available here) — verify before wiring into editors/zed or vscode launch configs. gdb/Windows explicitly out of scope (phase 1 = lldb/Linux, per the plan).

cards.title: Full HTTP core library — client + server (D-NETDEP1=A, owner-expanded mandate)
cards.body: Owner mandate (2026-06-26, expanding D-NETDEP1=A): Jet ships a full, complete HTTP library — both client AND server — as a core library, better than Go's net/http. D-NETDEP1's approved pure-Rust crate (ureq/minreq) is only the BOOTSTRAP backing c157's build-time fetch(url, sha256:); the native-ize end-state (Epoch-3 dep rule) is a first-party Jet/Rust HTTP stdlib. SCOPE: client (request/response, methods, headers, body, streaming, TLS, redirects, timeouts) + server (listener, router, handler, middleware, request/response types, graceful shutdown). The client+server API surface (naming + shapes) is SYNTAX/stdlib-surface design needing its own decision docs + ballots BEFORE code — drive from a real-world example per owner-anti-repetition + owner-decision-doc-style. NOT this card: c157's fetch backend (ships first against the bootstrap crate).
cards.plan: Umbrella reconciliation, not a second HTTP build. Treat #300 as the socket/DNS prerequisite and #301 as the canonical core.http implementation. Verify #301 against D-HTTPLIB1-4 plus current canon: HTTP/1.1 depth here, HTTP/2 as transport upgrade, WebSocket in core.ws, rustls TLS, function-first mux, split client/server. Remove any stale duplicate backend or bootstrap claim. Close only after the dependent cards prove streaming, redirects, timeouts, graceful shutdown, hostile protocol inputs, Jet-owned diagnostics, examples/goldens, and AOT/dev parity.

Clear error if the binary is run outside jet dev. (2) for_app(path) now canonicalizes relative-or-absolute against invocation cwd up front. (3) .html(path) already resolved against the app files dir (matches #Html semantics); absolute paths pass through via Path::join. Fix: run_dev_entry passes its own current_exe() as JET_BIN; DevServer prefers JET_BIN over PATH. 196s dev() is now just devserver.app() + serve(). Big pivot per owner: dev-server config moves from CLI flags/file-top markers into real Jet code. Built fn dev() as a well-known optional entry point (like main, no new syntax): jet dev <file> checks for it first; if present, compiles the file NATIVELY with dev() swapped in as the real entry (AST-level rename before codegen, reusing the same you-can-swap-entry idea as jet test/jet bench, not a new CompileMode), runs the resulting binary, and dev()s own Jet code configures+starts a real core.devserver value (devserver.for_app(file).html(...).port(...).serve()). The running compiled program cant link the compiler, so serve() shells out to jet build --target=web for every rebuild (subprocess, not a library call) -- new Prelude/DevServer.rs, std-only. If no fn dev() exists, falls straight through to todays default (jet dev --target=web / #Target(Web) inference), unchanged -- verified via the pre-existing test suite untouched.

Found + fixed a real ordering bug during my own verification (not caught by the automated test, which used a fixture without #Target(Web)): the #Target(Web)-inferred built-in server check ran BEFORE the fn dev() check, so any file with both markers -- e.g. 196, which already had #Target(Web) from earlier this session -- could never actually reach the new path; it silently fell back to the old built-in server every time, looking identical from the outside (same port, same content served). Reordered so fn dev() is checked first (more specific override wins). Verified for real this time by checking the process tree for the actual compiled child binary + confirming a live jet build subprocess-driven rebuild-on-save, not just that a server responded on the port.

cards.title: Next-generation FFI: one structure for every foreign language
cards.body: Owner directive (2026-07-02): reopen FFI structure with the bar set at revolutionary UX/DX — it should be almost trivial to use almost any other language as a wrapper/binding, so in-situ replacements are easy and Jet can tap ALL developments of other ecosystems immediately. This ballot picks the shared architecture (surface law); per-language depth (binder strategy for Python, JS, Swift, …) follows as one ballot each on that frame. Existing ratifications are inputs, not casualties: S50 (extern rust), S59 (C namespaces + bindgen/overlay — already the C instance of the recommended shape), D-NPMTYPE1 (typed npm stubs), D-JSWIFTFFI1 (JS first, Swift via C-ABI later). Ballot D-FFI-UNIFY1 attached.
cards.plan: Use D-FFI-UNIFY1=A as one foreign-namespace architecture: generated typed stubs and binders feed a common checked FFI boundary, while each language adapter owns transport details. Finish canonical descriptor, ownership/error/layout conversion, safe-vs-#Unsafe boundary, build/cache/provenance, package provider integration, and per-language capability reporting. Reconcile Python A, external provider A, existing C/Rust/npm/JS/Swift law, and active polyglot phase cards. Keep compiler seams dependency-free; foreign dependencies live in generated bridge/runtime packages.

cards.title: CI and quality gates — the professional bar
cards.body: Audit 2026-07-05: CI runs 5 of ~70 test targets (lib, truthfulness, diagnostic_snapshots, golden, cross) — lsp, fmt, repl, jetpack, workspace, web_build, ownership etc. never run on PR. CI also still calls frozen tools/Tower/Tower.mjs (MOVED.md says don't). No clippy/rustfmt/warning gate; no perf-regression or fuzz cadence. Decisions: D-CI1 gate composition, D-CI2 warning policy.
cards.plan: Implement D-CI1=A and D-CI2=A as the single authoritative CI contract. The current workflow already invokes the full verifier and nightly fuzz/perf pieces; reuse those jobs, do not create a parallel full-suite law. Every proposed change runs the complete executable suite on the exact candidate revision. Sharding may reduce wall time only: maintain a checked inventory mapping every tests/*.rs target exactly once and a completeness gate that fails on omission or duplication. Add required grammar-drift proof using tests/grammar.rs and a deterministic documentation-build gate covering links, doctests, stale examples, and the currently ratified documentation command behavior without reopening deferred D-DOC-GEN1 implementation. Add rustfmt, curated correctness/suspicious clippy, and Linux/macOS -Dwarnings; every intentional #[expect] has a live #card reason and fails when unfulfilled. Use only live read-only Tower lint/status paths; CI receives no board-write authority. Nightly adds the supported Linux/macOS full-suite matrix, pinned performance regression harness and ratchets, bounded rotating-seed fuzz cadence, and coverage artifact plus ratchet floor. Preserve seed, toolchain, candidate revision, shard map, test list, coverage, benchmark samples, and run URLs as durable artifacts. Prove the perf ratchet with an injected regression then exact restoration, and prove change-gate completeness with a throwaway canary failure then restoration. Remove obsolete tools/Tower teaching and fold the D-CI3 workflow comment into D-CI1 rather than maintaining two competing laws. No compiler dependency or owner gate.

Linux and macOS change jobs pass rustfmt, curated correctness/suspicious clippy, and -Dwarnings; every #[expect] has a live #card reason and unfulfilled expectations fail.
CI uses only the live Tower CLI for read-only lint/status and has no board-write credentials or automatic card mutation; obsolete tools/Tower paths are absent.

A temporary performance regression makes the ratchet fail and exact restoration makes it pass; a temporary formerly-uncovered test failure makes the change gate fail and exact restoration makes it pass.

cards.title: Bootstrap readiness gate: dogfood portfolio + memory-model soundness campaign
cards.body:
HARD GATE for e8 — no port work starts until this card is done and owner signs off. Core lang must be locked-happy (stdlib may still flux).

Evidence required:
1. **Dogfood portfolio** — enough real example projects in Jet, chosen for fringe needs and complexity, to stress the language end-to-end: compiler-shaped programs (formatter port, interpreter, arena/index-handle AST work), long-lived concurrent services, comptime-heavy code, FFI-heavy code, large multi-package workspaces. Each project reviewed for (a) readability and (b) how well an agent/human can reason about the codebase cold.
2. **Memory-model soundness campaign** — adversarial stress of memory model v5 (D-MEM1: bare/read, &/write, ^/take, second-class borrows) to Rust-borrow-checker confidence: soundness test suite, fuzzing, differential testing vs rustc on generated code, deliberate escape attempts (use-after-take, aliasing writes, arena dangling-index patterns), and I1 audit that no safe-Jet program can reach UB. Exit = virtually 100% certainty it is as solid as Rust.
3. **Syntax/coverage sweep** — every ratified surface feature exercised in the portfolio; gaps become examples or ballots.
4. **Owner sign-off ballot** — final "core lang is frozen enough to port" decision, minted when evidence is assembled.

Blocks the full-port card.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.files/core.path — file I/O parity with pathlib/Go os/Rust fs

Best-in-class bar: Python pathlib ergonomics, Go os robustness, Rust std::fs safety. Card #58 (path objects, atomic write, dir-walk) is done — first verify what actually shipped vs docs/reference/core-library.md (the doc shows no walk/glob/metadata), then close the residual gaps so core.files is a strict superset of the bar.

Gaps to audit and close: file metadata (size, mtime, created, permissions, file type) as a typed Stat value; create_dir_all / remove_dir / remove_all; glob patterns and recursive walk with entry filtering; symlink create/read/detect and hardlinks; temp files and temp dirs with RAII cleanup; atomic write (verify #58); advisory file locking; canonicalize/absolute; copy_dir tree; seek/offset reads and byte-stream (non-line) buffered readers/writers; fsync/flush-to-disk; filesystem watch (notify events) — watch may deserve its own module name (ballot).

Done means: every gap either ships with example + golden test, or is recorded as an owner-declined non-goal in the stdlib map. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).
cards.plan: Current source already ships D-FSOPS1, D-FSWATCH1, and the owners D-WATCH-SCOPE1 comment: core.watcher owns file, process, and port handles; core.event scopes own callbacks; core.files/core.path own filesystem operations. Do not rebuild or rename this surface. Remaining closure is proof and truth reconciliation. First run the existing files_depth and watcher goldens plus corelib, parity, and path_durability tests against the production prelude. Verify the watcher example exercises recursive file changes, process exit, port readiness, WatchSet composition, scoped callbacks, cancellation/drop, and documented std-only polling fidelity without shell polling or silent platform claims. Obtain native Windows evidence for lexical path normalization and write_atomic replacement/durability already met on Linux; preserve collision-safe temp cleanup and permission behavior. Audit docs/reference/core-library.md and syntax-decisions against the actual core.watcher names and Event callback law. If any behavior is missing, repair the single existing implementation in FsIoEnvOsTesting.rs and ReactiveEventWatch.rs; add no alias, module, dependency, or new ballot. A different reviewer validates native evidence and every remaining criterion before closure.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.text — Unicode completeness (case folding, segmentation, width)
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Swift String honesty + ICU floor. Cards #66 (graphemes, normalization) and the unicode slice of #117 are done — verify shipped surface first.

Audit list: NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD normalization (verify); full Unicode case mapping and case folding for upper/lower/caseless-compare (not ASCII-only); grapheme iteration (verify) plus word and sentence segmentation (UAX #29); display width (east-asian width) for terminal alignment; char classification (alphabetic, numeric, whitespace per Unicode); efficient String builder for heavy concatenation; general str utility audit vs Rust str + Python str (splitn/rsplit, trim variants, pad/center, starts/ends combinators, char_indices equivalents). Collation/locale sort: record policy (probably an i18n non-goal for now — state it).

Done means: audit table in docs, gaps shipped with examples + golden tests or recorded as declined non-goals. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).
cards.plan: Finish D-TEXTUNICODE1=A with core.text as the single Unicode algorithm home and String-aware tooling inserting those calls. Verify/complete NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD, full case mapping/folding, grapheme/word/sentence segmentation, D-TEXTWIDTH1=B display width, classification, scalar/UTF-8 helpers, and efficient builder/util parity. Pin Unicode data/version and deterministic behavior; state collation/locale policy explicitly. Prove hostile ill-formed boundaries, large text, AOT/dev parity, docs/examples, and Core rubric status.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.net — socket layer parity with Go net
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Go net — the lauded gold standard. A core.net namespace exists in the prelude; audit its real surface first.

Scope: TCP dial/listen/accept with deadlines and typed addresses; UDP send/receive; Unix domain sockets; DNS resolution (A/AAAA, SRV, TXT) with timeout control; IpAddr/SocketAddr as typed values (not strings); TLS client stream over any socket (reuse the D-TLS1 bridge); dual-stack/happy-eyeballs dialing; graceful close semantics; integration with core.tasks deadlines (#Context budget observed by blocking socket ops, like tasks.join already does).

Done means: an echo server + client example pair ships with golden tests; surface documented in core-library.md. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).

Implement D-NETDNS2, typed addresses, dual-stack/happy-eyeballs, deadlines/cancellation, task parking, backpressure, graceful close, and TLS streams under the single structured IOError tree. Honor D-NETIO1=D and NETIO contract outcomes exactly; never silently block scheduler workers. Prove real loopback TCP/UDP/Unix/DNS/TLS, partial I/O, timeout/cancel/race, IPv4/IPv6, AOT/dev parity, examples/docs, and no orphan blocker.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.http — client/server parity with Go net/http + requests ergonomics
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Go net/http server completeness with Python requests/httpx client ergonomics. Client HTTPS-by-default (D-TLS1) and server TLS (D-TLSSERVE1) shipped — audit the rest.

Client gaps to audit: connection pooling/keep-alive; redirect policy control; cookie jar; multipart upload and form encoding; streaming request and response bodies (bounded memory); per-phase timeouts (connect/read/total); proxy support (env-standard); transparent gzip decompression; HTTP/2; typed URL input (consumes the core.url card).

Server gaps to audit: router with path params and wildcards; middleware chain; streaming responses and server-sent events; graceful shutdown; request size/time limits (safe defaults — I1); static file serving with range requests; access logging via core.log.

WebSocket client + server: likely its own module name (owner ballot). Done means: audit table plus shipped gaps with example servers/clients under golden tests; a realistic REST service example needs no third-party anything. cards.title: corelib audit: core.crypto — misuse-resistant suite (AEAD, signatures, KDF, password hashing)
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: libsodium/age misuse-resistance — high-level envelopes a beginner cannot hold wrong, primitives behind them for experts. Card #64 (crypto push) is done — but the prelude currently exposes only sha256, hmac, and random_bytes; verify what actually shipped (FFI bridge included), then close the gaps.

Scope: authenticated encryption seal/open envelope with one canonical cipher (XChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-GCM — owner ballot), nonce handling internal (never user-supplied by default); Ed25519 sign/verify; X25519 key exchange; Argon2id password hash + verify with safe defaults; HKDF; SHA-512 and BLAKE3; constant-time comparison; key/secret types that refuse Display (no keys in logs — safe by default); simple key encoding (raw/hex/PEM as needed); file-encryption envelope (age-class). PQ hybrid agility already tracked (#71).

I6: implementations in-house or behind the FFI bridge crate — each new bridge dep is an owner ballot. Done means: each primitive ships with test vectors from the reference specs (RFC/NIST/libsodium vectors) as golden tests. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).

cards.title: Canvas requirement: multiple execution pins IN and OUT on nodes
cards.body: OWNER REQUIREMENT (2026-07-09, verbatim): 'multiple execution pins BOTH in and out SHOULD NOT be impossible, those are requirements for functional parity with blueprint.' Multi-exec-OUT partially exists (branch then/else, pattern arms); must generalize: any control construct with N outgoing paths projects N labeled exec outs (switch arms, loop body/done, early returns). Multi-exec-IN needs design: in Blueprint any node accepts multiple incoming exec wires (execution converges); in source-backed Jet a statement executes wherever control reaches it — N incoming exec wires = N call/reach sites of the same statement span, which today's projection renders as one exec-in accepting only one wire. Design task: projection + wiring transactions letting multiple exec sources target one node (shared continuation = e.g. moving the target into a helper fn Canvas auto-extracts, or a labeled block both paths jump to). If a canonical mechanism needs new syntax or an auto-extract convention, STOP and raise a ballot (I8: one mechanism). Deliverable: design note under docs/plans/epoch-6/ + ballot if gated + implementation with interaction scenarios (wire two exec outs into one node, assert source + execution).

cards.title: R12 parity: comptime/REPL tier-0 missing BigInt (E0956) — audit full builtin surface
cards.body:
Owner hit this live (2026-07-09): `big :: BigInt(100)` in jet repl fails with E0956 "calling BigInt can't run at compile time yet", while examples/features/text/bigint.jet (D-BIGINT1=A, golden) runs fine AOT. The REPL executes through the comptime interpreter (tier-0), so every builtin the AOT backend supports but comptime doesn't is a user-visible parity break — R12 requires JIT/dev/REPL parity through the same executable TIR.

Scope:
1. Implement BigInt construction + arithmetic + to_string in the comptime interpreter (crates/jet-comptime; CtValue may need a BigInt variant — check how AOT lowers it first).
2. Audit: enumerate every builtin/Core call AOT supports vs the comptime whitelist; produce the parity matrix as a test (ui or dedicated tests/parity.rs) so new builtins can't ship AOT-only. E0956 sites are the search key.
3. Each fixed gap needs a repl transcript test; keep E0956 wording for genuinely impossible-at-comptime effects only.

Repro: printf 'big :: BigInt(100)\n:quit\n' | target/debug/jet repl

cards.title: E4-JP3 Real Linux/macOS/Windows build sandbox
cards.body: Replace sandbox-status facade with enforced OS isolation. Linux namespaces/private proc-dev/read-only inputs; macOS sandbox policy; Windows restricted token/Job Object/ACL projection; network only for fixed-output fetch. Hostile corpus is binding.
cards.plan: D-JPK-EPOCHBOUNDARY1=B makes this Epoch 8 card the sole complete hostile Linux/macOS/Windows package-isolation proof and full-isolation claim. Reuse the current RuntimePolicy and Recipe action seams, but replace detection/ordinary Command execution with one runner that enters the real boundary before untrusted code. Linux uses namespaces, private proc/dev, read-only inputs, writable scratch/output, no-new-privileges, and network only for fixed-output fetch. macOS uses a native sandbox profile with the same file, process, device, and network authority. Windows launches under a capability-less AppContainer token with no internetClient, privateNetworkClientServer, enterpriseAuthentication, broadFileSystemAccess, or device capability; ACL-project only declared read inputs and writable scratch/output, place the whole descendant tree in a kill-on-close Job Object, and scrub inheritable handles and environment. Prove Windows network denial explicitly with hostile loopback, LAN, DNS, and public TCP/UDP attempts, plus child escape and handle smuggling; a status flag or restricted token alone is not isolation. Apply D-JPK-SANDBOX2=D exactly: non-executing copy/prebuilt verification may proceed; fetched/transitive executable actions require strong confinement, then a trusted substitute or approved remote builder, then fail closed. Exact digest/capability/reviewer/expiry local first-party grants remain audited, private, untrusted, non-publishable, and never widen Windows AppContainer/network authority silently. One shared native corpus attacks paths, symlinks, host/sibling writes, undeclared executables, ptrace/devices, network, child/daemon escape, cancellation, crash cleanup, and false status on all three OSes. Human/JSON/dossier/docs report only the boundary actually entered. Independent platform review gates the full-isolation claim. Ballot first for any new syntax/dependency.

Native macOS sandbox profile enforces the same file/process/device/network authority and resists the same hostile corpus without status-only or model-only proof.

Native Windows executes every hostile recipe inside a capability-less AppContainer token with ACL-projected inputs/scratch/output, kill-on-close Job Object, scrubbed handles/environment, and no network capabilities; loopback, LAN, DNS, public TCP/UDP, child escape, and handle-smuggling attacks all fail at the OS boundary.

D-JPK-SANDBOX2 substitute-first/fail-closed law is end-to-end: non-executing steps proceed, executable steps require strong isolation or trusted substitute/remote builder, and local grants remain digest/capability/reviewer/expiry-bound private untrusted outputs.
No command, JSON, dossier, cache record, or audit path reports sandboxed unless the named OS primitive was entered successfully; failure and cleanup are Jet-owned and deterministic.

cards.title: jetpack: leases with executables unusable on macOS/Windows — create_exec_wrappers returns Err on non-Linux
cards.body: Found during #465 burndown (jetpack-jail cluster). crates/jetpack/src/Store.rs:931-939: the #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))] create_exec_wrappers unconditionally returns Err whenever a lease contains executables, so snapshot_lease — mandatory for every consumer since #418 — fails at runtime on macOS/Windows for any package with a bin/. Distinct from the platform-lane COMPILE failures already tracked on #465 (deny(warnings) unused imports + E0277 in Store.rs:605): this is a runtime gap that survives the compile fix. Needs a real non-Linux exec-wrapper strategy (or explicitly documented platform contract), plus platform-lane test coverage. Also note tests/jetpack.rs parent_env_unchanged_after_run now asserts the Linux /proc/self/fd wrapper head — gate or branch that assertion when non-Linux wrappers land.
cards.plan: Preserve commit 884df04d for non-Linux empty/data-only leases and the Linux private read-only mount. D-JPK-EXECLEASE1=A fixes the remaining design. This card owns new product artifacts; no existing packaging/service seam is assumed. Add a narrowly scoped jetpack executable-lease client/service protocol, a root-owned macOS service binary plus signed installer package and LaunchDaemon plist, and a Windows service binary plus signed MSI/service registration and uninstall path. One explicit administrator approval installs them. Authenticate only local callers. In the service privilege domain, reopen the locked object, independently verify digest and executable identity, copy bytes to a caller-unwritable protected lease directory, then launch under the caller UID/session/token with no root/SYSTEM privileges, service handles, privilege-sensitive environment, mutable package path, or network capability. Protected lease bins precede only approved inherited/system PATH. The service never resolves packages, evaluates source, builds arbitrary requests, or accesses network; native loopback/LAN/DNS/public socket attacks must fail. Bind the shell and every descendant to lease lifetime; revoke/delete on normal exit, cancellation, crash, disconnect, timeout, service restart, uninstall, and reboot recovery. Direct jetpack run and nested jet env PATH execution resist rename, symlink, hardlink, content, directory, and time-of-check/time-of-use swaps. Reserve unused E1300 as the dedicated executable-lease service diagnostic family entry, with exact what/why/fix, JSON projection, `jet explain`, and snapshots for missing/stopped service, authentication failure, unverifiable bytes, failed isolation/network denial, and cleanup failure; E1292 remains package-signing entropy only. Doctor/audit names service/toolchain version, caller/child identity, stripped authority, PATH, network denial, verified handoff, and same-user redirect protection. Native Ubuntu regression plus macOS/Windows install/service/hostile runtime CI and independent review close the card. Ballot first for new syntax/dependency.

Eight transplants with placement verdicts: D-BINPAT1 (Erlang bit syntax as binary patterns in the one pattern engine — core language), D-STM1 (#Transact gains composable atomic commits across Shared<T> — core language), D-AUTH1 (core.auth batteries: sessions/password/OAuth/magic links — core lib), D-SYNC1 (core.sync CRDT value types riding live queries — core lib), D-VALIDATE1 (accumulated typed validation over decode/refinements, struct-is-the-schema — core lib), D-DBPOLICY1 (Supabase-RLS-class row policies checked vs live-query paths — core lib/safety), D-ENVHOOK1 (direnv-style opt-in env auto-activation — tooling), D-OBSERVE-LIVE1 (Erlang-observer-class live task/channel/deadline inspector — tooling). Rejections and already-have-its were preserved in current law before proposal retirement.
cards.plan: Finish only open ratified slices; do not rebuild verified STM, validation, env-hook, binary-pattern, or observer work. First complete D-AUTH2/D-AUTH-TOKENPOLICY1 standalone JWT and PASETO verification with required audience, trust/key policy, credential taint, hostile tokens, examples, and AOT/dev parity. Keep full app.auth sessions/OAuth/magic links blocked on #438 plus email substrate. Implement D-SYNC1 and D-DBPOLICY1 only through their canonical live-query/app graph cards; reconcile results here. Close after every criterion is independently verified and proposal/docs stop claiming unbuilt legs.

cards.title: Polyglot Phase 5: enterprise estates — COM/VBA, PowerShell, Dart, Tcl, Ada, Pascal
cards.body: From docs/proposals/polyglot.md Phase 5. Six binder ballots on the D-FFI-UNIFY1 structure: D-FFI-COM1 (Windows COM/IDispatch automation — the Office VBA estate, typed stubs from type libraries), D-FFI-PWSH1 (sidecar pwsh worker, objects as DataTree), D-FFI-DART1 (dart FFI + Flutter embedding), D-FFI-TCL1 (in-process interp, EDA estate), D-FFI-ADA1 (GNAT C-ABI, defense/avionics, pairs with jet prove), D-FFI-PASCAL1 (FreePascal C-ABI). ABAP/RPG/PL-I/JCL stay gateway-only until a real engagement demands a root; importer framework (D-MIGRATE-SRC1) leads there.
cards.plan: Implement COM/VBA, PowerShell, Dart, Tcl, Ada, and Pascal as language adapters on D-FFI-UNIFY1, not separate compiler paths. Generate typed stubs from native metadata where available; define value/error/ownership/callback/process/thread conversions; isolate sidecars; capture toolchain/package/cache/provenance; and report exact capabilities. Prove one real end-to-end workflow plus hostile failure per adapter on its supported platform. ABAP/RPG/PL-I/JCL remain gateway/import-only until separately ratified.

Preserve D-VERDICT-666-1: one compiler core and exactly two feature-identical lenses, JIT for rapid development and AOT for shipped binaries. First record one authoritative numeric and hostile-data policy for empty reducers, NaN and infinity, signed zero, quantile domain and interpolation, variance convention, rolling width, overflow and precision, pivot key identity, and negative or non-finite plots; coordinate typed runtime failures with #707. Then add failing hostile AOT tests for every law, fix only the shared native implementations, and extend the flagship example and normative docs. After #728 removes transparent AOT fallback and #729 lowers core calls, run the same cases through strict resident JIT with backend trace and compare stdout, stderr, exit status, shapes, ordering, missingness, and failures. Finish with scoped verification and independent review. Add no syntax, dependency, DataFrame facade, provider bridge, or duplicate algorithm.

log.text: Audit only; no source edits. Shipped AOT floor already includes typed table and series wrappers, schema, CSV and JSON ingest, stable filter and sort, deferred lazy plans, stable typed joins with duplicate multiplicity, grouping and aggregate stats, pivot, rolling mean, status, and text or SVG bars. Hostile gaps remain exact: empty stats return 0.0; quantile clamps out-of-range q; rolling width coerces zero to one; NaN and infinity ordering is not normative; pivot keys concatenate row and column with a delimiter and can collide; SVG bars can emit negative widths; current tests do not prove these laws. Strict resident-JIT parity is unavailable because the core calls or const-inline family remains a #729 gap and current default dev can hide it with the #728 AOT fallback. Required Jet-environment tests could not be rerun because this session cannot access the local Nix daemon. Relevant compiler surface and docs paths are already dirty or foreign-owned, so no isolated authorized family was safe to implement.

criteria.text: Typed Table, Series, and schema operations execute natively through the single ratified core.data facade across ingest, selection, join, group, aggregate, stats, and plot; no fixture-only or second DataFrame mechanism.

Filtering and sorting are stable; lazy plans remain deferred until materialization; inner joins preserve full duplicate-key multiplicity and left and right input order; left joins preserve every left row with None for unmatched right rows; groups, pivots, and windows have deterministic collision-free keys and ordering.

Missingness is represented only by typed optional values, including empty and generic schemas. Normative numeric laws cover empty input, NaN and infinity, signed zero, quantile domain and interpolation, variance convention, window width, overflow, and precision without silent sentinel values or coercion.

Deterministic first-party text and SVG plots escape hostile labels and define negative and non-finite values, bounds, and layout; data.status reports each native operation truthfully under D-DATA-PLOT1 and D-DATA-STATUS1.

Every operation has strict AOT and resident-JIT differential proof for stdout, stderr, exit status, result shape, ordering, and failure behavior, with backend trace proving no AOT fallback; comptime parity is covered where the operation is const-eligible.

A hostile executable corpus covers empty and all-missing data, duplicate joins, delimiter-like pivot keys, unstable-key ties, extreme numeric values, invalid quantiles and windows, hostile plot labels, and large inputs; the flagship example, reference and spec text, independent review, and scoped verification match shipped behavior.

cards.title: Encoding: independent hostile-oracle review
cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #296 criterion 9. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #296 govern this slice.
cards.plan: Review starts only after every producer closes. #710 first resolves its open XML projection ballot and finishes XML. #711 hostile-stream and #712 edition-surface work can proceed in parallel. #713 then proves whole/stream and execution-tier parity on those final engines. #714 pins all official and hostile corpora, examples, goldens, docs, and diagnostics against the shipped behavior. #715 reviews the clean integrated range after #710 through #714 close; it does not repair producer code or certify partial work. Preserve earlier accepted checkpoints as scoped history, not final proof. Reviewer procedure: 1. Record authority, base and tip, producer identities, reviewer identity/model/effort, target facts, and clean status. Read the full integrated diff and map every #710-#714 criterion to implementation and test evidence. 2. Verify every corpus manifest before use. Check URL/version, license/notice, SHA-256, case count, transformation provenance, and test reachability. Separate published oracle vectors from local hostile cases. 3. Run published expected-value and byte vectors for JSON/JCS, CSV, XML/Namespaces/C14N, CBOR, and base encodings. Run an independent implementation for interoperable cases, record its exact version and command, and classify each variance by standard clause and selected profile. Product code gains no oracle dependency. 4. Trace tests to the production whole/stream engines, host I/O, allocator, terminal state, migration, tier, and diagnostic paths. Reject delimiter scanners, transcript comparison, generated-source substitution, fallback masking, and test-only codecs. 5. Run negative controls for omitted or changed corpus rows, bad hashes, wrong outputs, every hostile I/O fault, terminal-repeat drift, allocator and limit crossings, XML external access, migration drift, and backend substitution. Each control must make the named oracle red, then be removed. 6. Run every split up to 4096 bytes, 32 saved deterministic chunk plans above it, endpoint and overflow limits, and three clean repetitions per supported platform and tier. Preserve seeds, oracle/tool versions, outputs, first differences, and timings. 7. Report only concrete findings. Producers fix them. Reviewer rechecks material fixes, reruns exact affected proofs, then verifies #715 and parent #296 criterion 9 with commit-bound evidence.

cards.plan: Authority is D-VERDICT-687-1. Default jet run uses JIT. jet build and jet run --release use AOT. A JIT gap is a compiler defect, not a fallback. Current dispatch violates that law. Default jet run enters run_compile_cmd and builds native Rust. Default jet dev constructs CraneliftBackend over AotFallbackBackend over InterpreterBackend. Hot swap and restart use the same ladder. CraneliftBackend delegates on a missing program or any JIT compile error. AotFallbackBackend compiles and runs AOT, then uses the interpreter when AOT is unavailable. Interpreter.rs also reruns an E0953 JIT result through AOT. That retry can duplicate effects. Explicit jet dev --interpret correctly uses InterpreterBackend and E2201. No E2211 source, registry row, snapshot, explain entry, or CLI test exists. Use this exact diagnostic copy. What: Jet JIT has a compiler gap for this checked program. Why: jet run uses the JIT lens and does not hide a JIT compiler gap by running AOT. Fix: run jet build <file> and the binary for now, then report E2211 with the detail below. Detail: JIT gap in {function}: {reason}. Attach the entry function span when available. Keep raw Rust and rustc text hidden. Return exit 101 because the exit table defines compiler defects as ICE. A watching dev session prints E2211, keeps the last good state, and continues. One-shot dev and default run exit 101. --try-anyway applies only to interpreter E2201 and never bypasses E2211. Implement in one order. First change api_debug try_resident, hot_swap, and restart from Option to Result and preserve unsupported host, lowering, safety, compilation, and panic reasons. Then make CraneliftBackend strict and remove its fallback generic. Delete AotFallbackBackend and its native subprocess runner after all product callers move. Keep InterpreterBackend only for explicit --interpret. Remove the E0953 AOT retry. Route default run to the same strict Cranelift backend. Keep build and run --release on CmdCompile AOT. Update watch, restart, and swap so a failed edit retains the last good runtime. Register E2211 under the JIT diagnostics area. Add the exact what, why, and fix row. Update the stale dev-loop prose. Add a rendered tests/dev/jit_gap.txt snapshot and generated error reference. Test supported JIT run, each gap class, unsupported host, no duplicate effects, watch recovery, one-shot exit 101, JSON, color, NO_COLOR, explain, default run, build, release run, and explicit interpreter. Re-run the #727 strict corpus gate. Do not add a daemon, alternate runner, new cache, or runtime AOT fallback.

cards.title: JIT: lower every native executable TIR form
cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #688 criterion 3. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #688 govern this slice.
cards.plan:
Amended 2026-07-24 after D-ONECORE1=A: this card is now the tier-1 performance ratchet, not a completeness gate. Sequence:
1. Finish the ABI/value-layout fidelity slice already in hand (parameter types, verifier mismatches, return typing) — that work is tier-1 correctness and survives the rework.
2. Then pause new gap classes until #776 lands the structured semantic-core TIR; string-parsing workarounds written against today's Rust-text TIR would be thrown away.
3. Resume on the new core, widening native coverage family by family in the #729 plan order, guided by tier-0/tier-1 timing from #778's --trace-tiers.
4. Every family keeps the differential proof (stdout/stderr/exit identical to AOT) and shrinks tests/jit_gaps.txt in the same diff.

First-reason families are core call 51; Result status 48; parameter type 20; comptime/const inline 19; cleanup/fallback 12; for-in 11; builtin method 10; call wrapper 7; enum payload/pattern 7; handle method 7; call resolution 6; closure 6; place/borrow 6; aggregate/list/map 5; require/panic/stop 5; unsafe 5; verifier/type mismatch 4; static constructor 4; binary 3; clone 3; returns 2; if-let 2; math 2; no runnable zero-param entry 2; string interpolation 2; transaction 2; and 1 each context, extern, fan-out, layout, field, numeric origin, precise numeric, print, struct destructure, todo, unary. criteria.text: Perf goal (amended by D-ONECORE1=A): every executable TIR form native AOT emits gains a Cranelift lowering over time. An unsupported form deopts to the interpreter (#778); it is never a user-facing failure. Zero gaps is the ratchet target, not a release gate.
Each JIT host shim calls the existing jet-foundation or runtime source of truth. It preserves types, effects, ownership, errors, traps, scheduling, and cleanup without a third algorithm copy.

The examples/features audit reports zero Cranelift verifier errors. tests/jit_gaps.txt is the complete deterministic inventory and shrinks monotonically; additions need a named reason in the same reviewed diff (D-ONECORE1=A ratchet).

Each lowering family has a JIT-to-AOT stdout, stderr, and exit-code differential test. Tier selection happens at function-compile time; a runtime failure occurs once and never retries another backend.
Cranelift lowers on every native host architecture Jet supports, including x86_64 and aarch64 on Linux, macOS, and Windows, or this card remains open.
Targeted lowerer, host-shim, corpus, and differential tests pass with independent review. The change adds no AOT fallback, alternate TIR, parallel runner, or duplicate cache.

cards.title: JIT/AOT: enforce parity in CI
cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #688 criterion 4. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #688 govern this slice.
cards.plan:
Amended 2026-07-24 after D-ONECORE1=A / D-LENS-RUN2=A. Prerequisites: #776-#778 replace the old #729-to-zero prerequisite; the gate ships with #778.
1. Restore the ratified D-CI3 triggers in .github/workflows/ci.yml (push, pull_request, nightly, workflow_dispatch); keep the full verify job.
2. Add one named parity job running #727's canonical command in three modes per case: pure-interpreter (tier 0), default tiered run, optimized AOT — byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit across all three. E2211 assertions are retired with #778.
3. tests/jit_gaps.txt is enforced as a shrink-only ratchet: additions need a named reason in the same reviewed diff; CI never rewrites it.
4. Native x86_64 and aarch64 runners for every host #729 proves; fail-fast false; 45-minute job limit; canonical reports uploaded with if: always() and 30-day retention.
5. Same strict job in release.yml; tag, test, and artifact commits must match.
6. Prove failure behavior with canaries (output mismatch, ratchet growth, timeout each make the job red), remove canaries, independent review, close.

log.text: Plan and criteria amended per D-ONECORE1=A / D-LENS-RUN2=A (sidequests #776-#779).

Release audit: .github/workflows/release.yml starts on version tags, builds Linux x86_64 and macOS x86_64 artifacts, uploads them, then publishes. It has no test or parity dependency, no Windows or aarch64 proof, no manifest or backend trace, and no failure artifact. Adding a workflow wrapper now would false-label incomplete tests. Card is blocked in order on #728 strict routing, #729 zero gaps and host support, and #727 final corpus runner and report.

Gate audit: jit_coverage_audit discovers 350 examples but only checks compile-set drift against tests/jit_gaps.txt. It accepts a nonzero known-gap list and does not execute the full strict AOT-runnable differential. Current measured run failed honestly: 87 covered, 262 gaps, one sema rejection, stale manifest 61/254; cold total 75.3s, test body 3.62s. cranelift_three_way_differential_battery covers only resident-safe examples with goldens, compares stdout rather than the full output triple, and can skip unsupported hosts. Current measured warm run aborted with stack overflow after 2m21s. Neither can be named the final parity gate.

CI audit: .github/workflows/ci.yml has only workflow_dispatch because automatic triggers are paused. Its 60-minute full verify job runs on ubuntu-latest x86_64 and includes all cargo tests, but it publishes no JIT parity artifact. The separate platform matrix tests Jetpack on Linux, macOS, and Windows; it does not test JIT/AOT parity. D-CI3=A still requires full verification on every push plus nightly fuzz and performance checks.

Reintegration: recovery WIP at stash 80bb80f1 is incomplete and parked, not landed. Missing TextUnicode source, codegen return typing, strict-lens diagnostic/call sites, argv wiring, and loop TIR support. Trial a2763bbe was reverted by 6762ddb3; no phase change.

criteria.text: CI runs the strict JIT-to-AOT differential gate on every push and pull request candidate. The nightly schedule also runs it. workflow_dispatch is not the only trigger.

The gate uses #727 as its only corpus and manifest owner. Every native AOT-runnable example has one result. Target-only exclusions name the target and reason. The gap manifest governs the tier-1 perf ratchet; output identity across tiers is the parity gate (D-ONECORE1=A).

Each case runs pure-interpreter, default tiered, and optimized AOT from the same commit. stdout, stderr, and exit code match byte for byte across all three. A skip, panic, timeout, missing result, or silent gap-manifest growth fails the job.
The CI matrix covers x86_64 and aarch64 on each supported native Linux, macOS, and Windows host. A platform can leave the matrix only when Jet no longer supports that native JIT host.

Corpus or classification drift fails. A reviewed lowering change can update the manifest in the same diff. It can remove a gap but cannot rebaseline a regression, add an unexplained exclusion, or auto-bless output.

Each matrix job has a 45-minute limit and uploads its commit, toolchain, target, case list, backend trace, output diff, result, and timing report for 30 days, including failed runs. Tagged release publication requires the same strict gate on the tagged commit.

cards.title: Deflake parallel child-build compiler-unlink stress test
cards.body: The Epoch 3 crypto/secrets closeout full suite failed once in tests/cli.rs::budget_parallel_child_builds_survive_running_compiler_unlink with divergent artifact hashes under full-suite load (expected a98b5986…, observed 369c208d…). Immediate exact isolated rerun passed 1/1 in 36.56s. Diagnose and make the stress test deterministic without weakening its unlink/parallel-build guarantee.

log.text: Accepted — closed (no formal ballot).

Ready for independent diff review and evidence rerun; not closed and no full suite run.

criteria.evidence: GPT-5.6 Sol/high independent adversarial review: reviewed #731 native_toolchain_identity and Linux stress-test hunks against 27165ba258802ee793b4064818fec311ab43461d; no concrete findings. Fixture primes one cache identity, launches two real budget children whose selected-artifact builds use that cache, unlinks and replaces compiler pathname with a different inode, verifies both signed reports against on-disk artifacts and the pinned hash/size. Final git diff -w --check passed.

cards.title: Sigil sweep: # for attributes/instructions/properties, @ for locations/addresses/sources
cards.body: Owner decree 2026-07-23: revert the rule/marker plane from @ back to #. Conceptual split: # marks attributes, instructions, properties; @ marks locations, addresses, sources. Reverses D-SHAPE2/D-MARKERMOVE1's @ plane; restores D-ATTR1's # plane. Highest priority: lands before any parallel in-flight syntax work to avoid rework.
cards.plan:
SCOPE (all gates ratified: D-VERDICT-732-1, D-ATTR4=A, D-LOOPLABEL3=A)
- Flip @ -> # for the whole applied-rule plane: RULE_PREFIX in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/markers.rs plus every APPLIED_RULES spelling (@Unsafe, @Test, @Pure, @Cli, @Task, @Every, @Target, @Pre/@Post/@Persist, @Inline/@InlineAlways, bundles, serde markers, @DebugOnly, @Meta, @[allow(...)], @[a,b] lists, pub-file/no-prelude/static/inline/SIMD-reduce rules).
- effects_surface.rs already holds ATTR_PREFIX="#" and FOREIGN_AT_ATTR="@" from D-ATTR1; those become authoritative again. Teaching-error direction reverses: @Marker in rule position -> 'attributes use #'.
- D-ATTR4=A: interpolation debug spec flips to {value#Debug}.
- D-LOOPLABEL3=A: loop labels leave @ entirely. New: outer :: loop naming (compile-time label kind in the ordinary namespace), outer.break()/outer.next() dot exits, bare break/next keywords keep working for the innermost loop. outer@ suffix + break outer@ retire with a teaching error; E0988 matrix updated; outer := loop rejected; label-in-value-position is a teaching error. expr ?? outer.break() composes per D-ORRETURN-CANON1.
- STAYS @ pending #733/D-JPK-REF1: provider@target source refs (U6), path@host OS selector (D-JPK-OSHOST1=C). Do NOT touch ref grammar in this card.
- STAYS #: [T#N] fixed-size separator (S76), #Caller(), textkit#1.2.0 version pins (VERSION-#).

FOOTPRINT (measured 2026-07-23): ~182 files with @-marker spellings across examples/docs/crates; docs/spec/diagnostics.md ~104 hits, syntax-decisions.md ~84, spec.md ~54, examples/canon.jet 18; examples/features/basics/labeled_loops.jet for D-LOOPLABEL3.

SLICES (each verified with targeted tests; full suite once at closeout)
1. Syntax registry: flip RULE_PREFIX to #, reconcile effects_surface constants, register :: loop-label form, update decision-ID comments.
2. Lexer/parser: # dispatch in rule position (decl/expr/scope); outer :: loop + dot-exit parsing; wrong-plane fall-throughs (#Wasm/#Js/#Suppress/#Uninit/#Ref retirements) keep behavior under the new prefix.
3. Teaching errors: @Marker -> use-# error; outer@/break outer@ -> use ::/dot-exit error; label-as-value error; each with UI snapshot (I4).
4. Formatter: emit # and :: labels; fmt STABILITY round-trip tests (idempotence alone misses dropped tokens).
5. Sema/LSP/highlights + editors/tree-sitter grammar (zed grammar-repo is generated, do not commit).
6. Sweep examples/**.jet + golden outputs (I5), canon.jet + labeled_loops.jet first; rm -rf ~/.cache/jet/build before smoke.
7. Docs sweep: syntax-decisions.md, spec.md, diagnostics.md, philosophy refs; UI snapshots re-blessed.
8. Closeout: fresh-binary smoke, one full-suite run, Sol review.

COORDINATION
- No other card may introduce @-plane or outer@-label spellings until this lands; in-flight branches rebase on the flip commit.
- Land slices 1-4 as one atomic sweep so no split-brain surface ships.
- Ref grammar (#733, D-JPK-REF1) is owner-gated and explicitly out of scope here.

cards.title: Ref shape conversion: package/source refs and host selectors
cards.body: Owner reopened the U6/D-JPK-OSHOST1 ref shapes 2026-07-23: provider@target and path@host don't feel right; wants something email-like (e.g. textkit#1.2.0@vendor). Gated on ballot D-JPK-REF1 (attached). Owner instruction: do not implement until ratified. Split out of #732 so the # marker sweep isn't held in the decide lane.
cards.plan:
GATE RATIFIED: D-JPK-REF1 = A (2026-07-23) — email order everywhere: name['#'version-or-channel]['@'source]. Amends U6/U9/D-JPK-OSHOST1.

THE NEW SHAPES
- deps: textkit: textkit#1.2.0 · pretty: textkit#1.2.0@vendor · helpers: ../helpers (bare ./ ../ / paths, no provider word; the 'path' provider name retires)
- sources: named source values flip to target@provider: vendor: acme/helpers@github; nixpkgs stays a bare provider source
- CLI refs: jetpack run fastfetch@nixpkgs (replaces <source>:<package> colon form)
- OS selector: jet os switch laptop@../machines (host@root replaces path@host; bare host unchanged)
- UNCHANGED: VERSION-# pins (textkit#1.2.0), channel refs #latest/#main (D-JPK-CHANNEL1), inline git structs (D-JPK23), provider inference by manifest probe (U9)

OWNED PATHS (measured 2026-07-23)
- crates/jet-pkg-model/src/RefSpec.rs (core parse), PackageManifest/ParseBlocks.rs + mod.rs, Merge.rs
- crates/jetpack/src/Provider.rs, CLI/add_remove_push_image.rs, JetOS/load_validate.rs, JetOS/nixos_import_live.rs
- crates/jet-env-model/src/ModuleEval/mod.rs
- crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/jetpack_config.rs (REF_PROVIDER_AT/OS_HOST_SELECTOR constants + decision comments)
- tests/jetpack_engine.rs, tests/pkg.rs, tests/jetpack_jetos.rs, tests/canvas.rs
- docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md (U6/U9/D-JPK-OSHOST1 sections), spec.md, diagnostics.md (E0968/E0979/E0981 what/why/fix text + snapshots)
- examples referencing refs

SLICES
1. RefSpec.rs: parse name[#ver][@source] atoms + target@provider source values + bare-path refs; old provider@target emits a teaching error naming the flip (I4, snapshot).
2. Manifest/CLI/OS consumers: ParseBlocks, Provider, CLI verbs, JetOS host selector (host@root), env-model eval.
3. Diagnostics: E0968/E0979/E0981 text rewritten to the new shapes; snapshots re-blessed.
4. Sweep tests/examples/docs; jetpack integration tests need cargo build -p jetpack --bin jetpack first (stale-bin trap).
5. Closeout: targeted suites (pkg, jetpack_engine, jetpack_jetos), Sol review.

COORDINATION
- Blocked by #732 (sigil sweep) — land after it; disjoint from #732's marker paths except docs/spec files, so rebase docs edits.
- Lock/manifest compatibility: no lockfile format change; only ref spelling parses differently. Old spelling = teaching error, not silent reinterpretation (github@owner/repo would otherwise parse as name 'github' at source 'owner/repo' — MUST be caught: a source value whose name matches a known provider word errors with the flip hint).

cards.title: Silent no-op: list element field writes are dropped
cards.body:
Ship-blocker from the 2026-07-23 persona audit (Klaus, systems dev).

Repro (/tmp/persona-klaus/mut.jet): `ps[0].x = 11` and `ps[0].x += 1` compile clean, mutate a temporary, and the old values print. Plain `ns[1] += 5` IS rejected with a teaching error — so the accepted spelling is the broken one.

This kills array-of-structs code (games, sims) with silent wrong physics. It breaks the spirit of I3: sema passes what codegen drops. Fix first, before any polish work.

log.text: Review finding — crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/statements.rs:41 and crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/statements.rs:822: indexed compound field assignment does not preserve Jet operator-hook semantics. Sema accepts hs[0].value += rhs when value implements Jet Add because compound_field_type cannot resolve Expr::Index; the new emitter then writes native Rust +=. Jet generates user_Add, not std::ops::AddAssign, so rustc rejects a sema-approved program, violating criterion 1 and I2. Repro check with a [Holder] whose Vec2 field implements Add reports no Jet problems. Fix by resolving and rewriting the indexed field hook through the existing Add method spine, or emit E0362 before TIR; add a regression for this indexed user-operator case. Numeric Int = and += paths pass targeted TIR, golden, strict interpreter/JIT/AOT three-way, fresh build/smoke, Pool parity, and columnar runtime/UI checks. Broad jit_coverage_audit still has known unrelated manifest drift; the new collections/struct_list_mutation entry is observed covered and IndexFieldAssign reports 2 covered, 0 gaps.
Master integration agent: do not stage, commit, or merge sidequests-implementation while these cards are active. Wait for explicit closeout handoff; sidequest workers own this worktree.

Investigation: parser and sema accept a mutable list-element field place, but TIR lowers the index through clone-returning jet_index_vec. AOT and default dev print old values. Forced interpreter gives E2201. Planned fix: use a bounds-checked mutable list place in shared TIR lowering; keep the interpreter teaching boundary.
Integration notice: implementation uses branch sidequests-implementation in .agent-worktrees/sidequests-implementation. Leave branch for the master integration agent after closeout.

cards.title: Diagnostics polish batch from the 2026-07-23 persona audit
cards.body:
Ten cheap diagnostic fixes found by the persona audit. Each is a wording, dedupe, or teaching gap — no new syntax, no owner decision.

1. `continue` gives E0003 (value not used) and never says Jet spells it `next`. Add a teaching error. Worst beginner trap found.
2. `?? { block }` is invalid and the fix text shows no working alternative.
3. The same E0107 appears twice for one span — dedupe.
4. A positional multi-payload variant `Hit(String, Int)` fails with a raw "expected `)`". Teach the S30 rule: one payload positional, two or more use named fields.
5. E0119 says "use `random.Rng` here" while E0112 rejects naming `random.Rng`; bare `Rng` works. Resolve the clash.
6. The `_` discard binding cascades into nonsense errors ("give away a copy instead (`~_`)").
7. `@Unsafe` with no reason gets lint L3101, and the same run prints "ok: no problems". The two statements clash.
8. L0504 flags `total := 0.0` as money. False positive.
9. E1004 leaks internal jargon ("documented M10 items").
10. `&particles[idx]` fix text teaches a copy that cannot change the list. Name the `&xs[a..b]` write-window idiom instead.

cards.title: Script-speed run loop: cached re-run, jet dev signpost, start budget
cards.body:
Persona audit 2026-07-23: every `jet run` costs 12-14s, even when the file did not change. `jet dev` runs the same file in 4.7s, but `jet run` never mentions it. Python starts at once. The focused agent audit also measured an unchanged process example at 36.38s through the required development environment. This gap decides the script persona and blocks Jet from replacing Bash, Python, and Node for short agent tasks.

Work:
- An unchanged file re-runs from cache with no recompile.
- `jet run` prints one tip line when a compile is slow: point at `jet dev`.
- Measure and enforce cold/warm script budgets against matched Bash, Python, and Node tasks.

Rides #687/#688 (jet run = JIT lens) and #439 (watch engine). The self-host era work (#666/#669) is the long game; this card owns the Epoch 3 daily-driver feel.
cards.plan:
Amended 2026-07-24: two facts change this card. First, the 2026-07-24 environment fix (batch-pass rewrite of scripts/agent/clean-nix-tmp.sh) removed a multi-minute shellHook stall; the recorded no-op baseline (jet-env true 57.826 s, cold 13.905 s, warm 12.088 s) is invalid — re-measure all spans before enforcing any budget. Second, D-ONECORE1=A / D-LENS-RUN2=A (#776-#778) make default jet run tiered; the interpreter tier needs no Cranelift compile, which changes the cold-start calculus.
Resume when #778 lands the tiered run path and #439 exposes the shared invalidation service. Put warm artifact reuse at the tier boundary: cache compiled tier-1 modules keyed by exact source, dependency, compiler-build identity, target, capability, and configuration facts; a hit skips load, parse, check, lowering, and code generation with trace proof. Do not extend the AOT BuildCache path or add another runner, cache, watcher, or daemon. Measure spans separately: environment entry; compiler startup; load; parse; check; TIR lowering; tier-1 compile; artifact load; program time. Add the slow-run signpost only in the common run coordinator (once, stderr, TTY-aware, NO_COLOR/JSON suppressed). Benchmark matched no-op, file/JSON, and subprocess fixtures against Bash, Python, and Node; record machine facts, cold and warm medians, and tail latency; enforce the ratified budget only after the method and value exist.

cards.title: Anonymous union types: decide before the stdlib bakes casts in
cards.body:
Promotes the union half of idea b4eclxq. The any half is ALREADY DECIDED: D-ANY-JAI1 (syntax-decisions.md:169-172) ratified trait-bounded heterogeneous varargs and rejected a general Any top type. That rejection is law and is not reopened here.

The open question: does Jet ever get anonymous union types (Int | String), or do named enums stay the only union? Why now (lessons-learned, Go generics): the encoding/data/web wave (#296/#307/#706-#709) is baking APIs that need the answer, and a missing type capability fossilizes casts into a stdlib.

Ballot D-UNIONTYPE1 on this card picks. Implementation follows ratification.
cards.plan: Implement ratified D-UNIONTYPE1=A as structural enum sugar, not a second sum mechanism. Add Type::Union with one canonicalizer that recursively flattens members, removes exact duplicates, and sorts by canonical source spelling; define parser precedence so T ? E1 | E2 places the union on the error side. Extend formatting, type traversal, equality/display, API snapshots, semantic index, and LSP to use that canonical form. In sema, allow only concrete closed member types, add implicit member-to-union widening at binding, argument, return, field, and error-propagation boundaries, and preserve exact union identity elsewhere. Extend union match heads to resolve an exact member type and feed the existing enum exhaustiveness and binding checks. Lower each canonical union to one deterministic compiler-generated enum emitted once per resolved union, with injection and match operations carried explicitly in TIR so codegen remains mechanical and native/web/dev agree. Extend Codable synthesis so each member encodes normally and decode selects a unique compatible wire shape; reject ambiguous or unsupported shapes in sema with registered UI diagnostics. Keep named-enum crossings explicit through ordinary match-based conversion functions and add no Any or cast escape. Update the syntax decision log and examples, regenerate grammar/tooling artifacts, bless snapshots, and run focused parser/formatter/sema/serde/golden plus AOT/dev/web parity checks.

log.text: Reconciled against ratified D-UNIONTYPE1=A and existing D-ANY-JAI1. The plan uses one enum mechanism, defines canonical structural identity and widening boundaries, makes Codable ambiguity a sema error, and keeps named-enum crossings explicit without adding conversion syntax. Card is implementation-ready; no owner decision remains.
Reconciliation 2026-07-23: re-scoped from union+any to union-only — D-ANY-JAI1 already rejects a general Any. Ballot id is D-UNIONTYPE1 (not D-ANYTYPE1).

syntax-decisions.md log entry
jet devtools grammars regenerated
snapshots re-blessed

D-UNIONTYPE1=A adds A | B in every type position as a closed structural sum; nested unions flatten, duplicate members disappear, and identity is order-insensitive with deterministic canonical spelling and codegen identity.

A member value widens implicitly into its union at binding, argument, return, Codable field, and ? error-propagation boundaries; T ? E1 | E2 parses as T ? (E1 | E2). Other implicit union-to-union or union-to-named-enum conversions are not introduced.

Matching names each member type as the arm head, binds the member value, rejects unknown or repeated member arms, and reuses the existing exhaustiveness mechanism so every normalized member is covered.

#[Codable] encode/decode supports union fields when every member supports the operation; decoding dispatches by wire shape and sema rejects ambiguous member shapes with a registered diagnostic instead of choosing by declaration order.

Named enums remain the stable public documenting form. Crossing between a union and a named enum is never implicit; docs demonstrate explicit match-based conversion functions in both directions under the existing destination-owned conversion law.

D-ANY-JAI1 remains intact: no Any/top type or unchecked cast path is added. Parser/formatter, sema, TIR/codegen, web/dev, semantic index/LSP, API snapshots, examples, UI/golden, and AOT/dev parity cover unions and diagnostics.

cards.title: Exclusive range spelling for index loops
cards.body:
Persona audit (Klaus): `..` is inclusive (S22, ratified, stays), so `0..1000` makes 1001 items and the common `0..len()` index loop panics at run time. The examples show no exclusive spelling.

Ballot D-RANGE-EXCL1 on this card decides: add an exclusive spelling, bless Jet-native idioms (sequence two-binding + `indexes`, pipeline `indexed`), or both. S22 inclusive-by-default is not reopened. Rec C would also amend D-ITER1 `enumerate` → `indexed`.
cards.plan: Implement ratified D-RANGE-EXCL1=C as one extension of the existing loop-range and collection-iteration paths. Add a registered ..< token and carry an inclusive/exclusive end mode through the loop AST, formatter, sema, TIR, native emitter, web/dev emitter, and semantic tokens; keep .. inclusive and keep the existing semicolon stride contract. Extend list and fixed-list source loops so two bindings receive index then item, while one binding remains item-only. Add the indexes sequence member through the existing builtin-member path and emit valid Int indexes only. In sema, recognize only the provable same-root shape where an inclusive loop ends at xs.len() and its body indexes xs; report a registered teaching diagnostic with the three ratified fixes and avoid heuristic lookalikes. Rename the public D-ITER1 adapter enumerate() to indexed() across sema, TIR, codegen, docs, examples, and tests, preserving the named tuple contract. Update the syntax decision log and examples, regenerate grammars, bless diagnostics, and run focused parser/formatter/UI/golden plus native/web/dev parity checks.

log.text: Read-only audit found no D-RANGE-EXCL1=C slice shipped. Lexer has only DotDot and DotDotDot. ForKind::Range carries no end mode and emit uses Rust ..= only. Sema has no same-root len/index teacher. Two-binding list loops are not typed or lowered as index/item. Lists expose no indexes member. The public adapter remains enumerate in foundation, sema, TIR, and codegen. No matching docs, examples, or tests exist. This is a broad parser-to-runtime change. crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/control.rs and crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Diagnostics.rs are staged by other work and stayed read-only.

Reconciled against ratified D-RANGE-EXCL1=C. The plan preserves S22 inclusive .., adds the exact half-open loop spelling, implements the provable teacher and safe sequence idioms, and applies the ratified D-ITER1 rename. Card is implementation-ready; no owner decision remains.
Refreshed D-RANGE-EXCL1: teach two-binding + indexes first; research favors indexed/with_index over enumerate; rec C amends D-ITER1 rename.

Sema reports a registered teaching diagnostic, with what/why/fix UI snapshot, only when it can prove that an inclusive loop ending at xs.len() indexes that same xs; fixes appear in the ratified order: two-binding loop, xs.indexes, then 0..<xs.len().

cards.title: Browser debugging: source maps for the web target
cards.body:
Field audit TypeScript row: the browser is the runtime and feedback is live. Jet ships a web/canvas target, but devtools cannot step Jet lines.

Work: emit source maps for the JS/Wasm output so browser devtools show and step Jet source. The compiler already maps Jet lines to generated Rust for diagnostics (Source/Compiler.rs SourceMap) — extend that chain to the browser. Rides the web wave (#123, #701-#705).

Flip test: set a breakpoint on a Jet line in browser devtools and step.
cards.plan: 1. Reuse `TStmt::LineMarker` for web output. Do not add a second source-location model. 2. Add a std-only Source Map v3 encoder with stable source order. Use UTF-16 columns for JavaScript. 3. Record generated JavaScript positions before each emitted TIR statement. Emit `app.js.map` and its relative `sourceMappingURL`. 4. Compile Wasm with line data. Read rustc's Wasm line table after compilation. Join generated Rust lines to Jet lines through existing markers. 5. Emit Wasm byte-offset mappings in `app.wasm.map`. Put the relative map URL in the Wasm `sourceMappingURL` custom section. 6. Default, debug, and CI web builds include exact Jet bytes in `sourcesContent`. Release builds emit no maps or map references. 7. Use project-relative source names with `/` separators. Never emit absolute host paths. 8. Add both map files to build output, atomic dev swaps, static serving, and last-good rebuild behavior. 9. Reuse the current Chromium CDP harness. Prove Jet breakpoints and stepping in JavaScript and Wasm. 10. Run focused web tests and fresh review. If Wasm decoding needs a new tool or crate, stop and raise a dependency ballot.

cards.title: Toolchain telemetry and trust policy
cards.body:
Lessons-learned gap 2 (2026-07-23): Go's telemetry episode and Audacity show that even well-intentioned opt-out telemetry burns trust permanently. Nothing on the board mentions telemetry — deciding it implicitly by code later is the expensive path.

Ballot D-TELEMETRY1 on this card decides: opt-in only vs none at all, and exactly what jet/jetpack may send over the network (registry queries included).
cards.plan:
Implement ratified D-TELEMETRY1=A and D-REPORT-SEND1=A only. No new owner choices.

1. Inventory every jet/jetpack network path. Prove builds and ordinary commands never open telemetry, crash, or usage endpoints.
2. Keep registry/package traffic limited to what the user-requested operation needs (name, version constraint, protocol necessities).
3. Ship or harden `jet report` as a local inspectable bundle writer that prints the path. Do not ship `jet report --send` (D-REPORT-SEND1 amends the illustrative telemetry example).
4. Document the permanent zero-telemetry promise in owner-facing tooling docs.
5. Add regression tests that fail if a background usage/crash sender appears, and CLI tests for local report bundle creation without network send.

Proof: focused CLI/tooling tests + greps/audit of network call sites. No full suite required for this card alone.
